title: LLM-based virtual screening identifies two NIR-II fluorophores tested in vitro and in vivo
summary: Researchers built a dataset of fluorophores emitting from visible to NIR-II and trained a large language model to predict maximum emission wavelength, which was competitive with conventional machine-learning and deep-learning baselines. Model-guided virtual screening prioritized NIR-II candidates, and two were experimentally characterized with favorable in vitro and in vivo imaging performance. These are imaging probes, not therapeutics.
ai_technology: Large language model for structure-property prediction, with virtual screening
organization: State Key Laboratory of Drug Research

evidence.tested: Two model-prioritized NIR-II fluorophores were experimentally characterized for imaging performance in vitro and in vivo.
evidence.unknown: Only two candidates were characterized; the abstract does not give quantitative brightness or penetration values; the work is about imaging agents, not drugs.
evidence.ai_role: A large language model predicted emission wavelengths and guided virtual screening to choose candidates.
